title: Duplicating a resource with invalid filename extension has "File name is valid", and also silently fails for non-imported resources
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot Engine v4.6.dev5.mono.official.f5918a9d3

### System information

Windows 10 D3D12 12_0 - Forward+ - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti

### Issue description

Duplicating a resource with invalid filename extension has "File name is valid" text and enabled "OK" button, but then (1) silently fails for non-imported resources, or (2) actually creates a duplicate which however doesn't appear at all in the editor (which is not what most users want or need arguably).

### Steps to reproduce

case (1)
* have any non-imported resource (imported data files like initial icon SVG *won't* do, it has to be tres/res-type one, e.g. empty scene will do)
* try to Ctrl+[D]uplicate the resource to open the Duplicating dialog
* change the extension to an invalid one (i.e. one that's neither res, tres nor the native type like "theme" or "material")
* dialog still says "File name is valid" in green
* click "OK"
* no file is created as a result, no error is reported anywhere
case (2)
* have any imported resource (initial icon SVG e.g.)
* try to Ctrl+[D]uplicate the resource to open the Duplicating dialog
* change the extension to an invalid one (i.e. one that's not SVG for the initial icon)
* dialog still says "File name is valid" in green
* click "OK"
* the file is created as a result, but understandably not shown in the editor (due to invalid extension), which is probably not what the user would expect or want (i.e. if the dialog says "filename is OK", it should be accessible in the editor afterwards, most probably just the extension that the file originally had)
